records.title: Cybersecurity technology — Assessment method for security capability maturity of artificial intelligence (draft for comment)

records.short_title: Draft national standard on AI security capability maturity assessment
records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260)
records.summary: Draft recommended national standard, proposed by TC260, that sets an AI security capability maturity model (ASMM) for assessing organisations, also usable by regulators as a reference. It covers data, model and application security in 15 activities and 39 process areas, such as red-blue adversarial testing, value benchmark testing, backdoor detection and emergency intervention. Each is rated on ten capabilities, among them robustness, explainability, fairness, rights protection and emerging-risk prevention, at five levels from informal execution to continuous optimisation, by self-assessment or a third party.
records.notes: TC260 opened the draft for comment on 26 Aug 2026, with comments due by 25 Oct 2026. The draft has no standard number yet (GB/T XXXXX—XXXX) and leaves its publication and implementation dates blank. Organisations are typed as data-support, model-technology or application-service bodies, and each process area is mandatory, conditionally mandatory or optional for each type; an organisation's level is the highest level that all its applicable process areas reach. At the top level for post-training security, safeguards such as blocking knowledge of biological weapons and cyberattacks must not be removed or significantly weakened when the model runs in agents. Normative references include GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10), GB 45438-2025 (CN-08) and GB/T 45674-2025.

records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: Draft TC260 practice guide on the secure development of agentic AI systems built on large models, covering the preparation, design, implementation, testing and release stages. It names risks such as prompt injection, goal deviation, privilege abuse, memory poisoning and cascading failure, and sets principles of risk orientation, graded control, human controllability and defence in depth. Measures include a risk register, models meeting GB/T 45654-2025, execution limits, rollback for irreversible operations, human confirmation, review and takeover of high-risk operations, guardrails, supply-chain checks, sandboxing, red-team testing and a pre-release security assessment.
records.notes: Released for public comment by the TC260 Secretariat with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕119号 of 18 Sept 2026; comments were due by 2 Oct 2026. The draft is version v1.0-202609 and carries the number TC260-PG-2026NA. It covers software agentic AI systems built on large models, not agentic systems whose main function is controlling physical devices such as robots or autonomous vehicles. Its bibliography lists AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 (CN-13) and TC260's practice guide on the security of deploying and using agents.

records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: General part of TC260's AI application security guidelines, for all sectors, based on the Cybersecurity, Data Security and Personal Information Protection Laws and the rules on generative AI, AI content labelling, algorithmic recommendation and deep synthesis. It sets principles such as ultimate human control and graded protection, and guidance for each stage from planning to decommissioning: risk identification, five-level security grading, capability maturity assessment, one-click takeover, emergency shutdown, safety tests (also for minors), guardrails, content labelling, emergency plans and annual re-testing; it encourages unconditional relief for major personal-injury accidents.
records.notes: Version v1.0-202609, released on 15 Sept 2026 with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕118号 together with sector guides for education, health, and radio, TV and network audiovisual services, to address new risks from the fast spread of AI applications. An organisation applying AI in a sector follows this guide and the sector document. The five security grades run from low to especially major security risk, and each party involved must reach a capability maturity level no lower than the application's grade; for grading and maturity assessment the guide refers to national standards on AI application security classification and grading and on AI security capability maturity. Normative references include GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10), GB 45438-2025 (CN-08), GB/T 45674-2025, GB/T 45652-2025 and TC260-005, AI Application Ethics Security Guidelines 1.0. Because responsibility for AI failures is hard to assign, it encourages arrangements in applications involving personal safety for immediate, unconditional humanitarian relief after major personal-injury accidents.

records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: Education guide in TC260's AI application security guidelines, used with the general part (TC260-PG-20268A). Educational institutions are to manage AI use by role, age and stage with whitelists, algorithm filing and security assessment, set up ethics review, and keep AI in an assisting role whose outputs people check, with notice, objection, human review and appeal channels. Minors need age-appropriate defaults, guardian consent and supervised use. Rules for AI-assisted teaching, learning, research, management and assessment include emergency takeover, a ban on AI-generated project applications, papers or research reports, and no negative evaluation of individuals.
records.notes: Version v1.0-202609, released on 15 Sept 2026 with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕118号 together with the general provisions and the health and audiovisual guides. It applies to educational institutions, defined as education administrative departments and their affiliated units and schools of all levels and types. Primary school pupils are not to use open-ended content generation alone, and important decisions on students, staff, resources and degrees are not to execute AI conclusions directly. Drafting units include the Ministry of Education's Department of Science, Technology and Informatization and its Education Management Information Center. Annex A describes typical scenarios and their main risks.

records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: Health guide in TC260's AI application security guidelines, for medical and health institutions and technology providers, used with the general part (TC260-PG-20268A). Doctors stay the decision-makers: AI diagnostic and treatment suggestions need a doctor's confirmation, patients must know of AI involvement and may refuse it, and applications need ethics committee review and filing with health authorities. It covers the life cycle and scenarios such as clinical decision support, triage (stopping the chat on emergency signs), public health warning and drug trials, and annexes a five-level risk grading.
records.notes: Version v1.0-202609, released on 15 Sept 2026 with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕118号 together with the general provisions and the education and audiovisual guides. The guide sets rules for dividing liability between doctors and AI when a system gives a wrong suggestion, and asks that systems be checked for performance across population subgroups, with restricted use where performance drops for groups such as children or the elderly. The informative annex grades AI applications in health as especially major, major, significant, general or low risk; the top grade has catastrophic and systemic features, and the annex refers to AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 (CN-13) for grading. Drafting units include the National Health Commission's Statistical Information Center.

records.summary: Guide for radio, TV and network audiovisual services in TC260's AI application security guidelines, issued with the NRTA Department of Science and Technology and used with the general part (TC260-PG-20268A). records.title: Cybersecurity technology — Generative artificial intelligence data annotation security specification
records.original_title: 网络安全技术 生成式人工智能数据标注安全规范
records.issuing_body: State Administration for Market Regulation / Standardization Administration of China (proposed and administered by TC260)
records.summary: Recommended national standard on the security of annotating training data for generative AI. It sets requirements for annotation platforms and tools (security assessments, logging, controlled work areas), for annotation rules (separate rules for functional and security annotation, spotting risky content, incident response), for annotators (security training and exams before qualification, defined roles, with different people executing and reviewing a task) and for verification: security annotations should cover the main risks in GB/T 45654-2025 Annex A, at least 200 items per risk and 3% of the data, and a batch is discarded when over 5% fail security checks.
records.notes: Published 25 Apr 2025 and effective 1 Nov 2025. It is a recommended 'GB/T' national standard, not a mandatory 'GB' one, and SAMR's platform lists a plan for an English-language edition. It takes its definitions of generative AI data annotation and of functional and security annotation from GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10), which names it as a companion standard. It applies to organisers of annotation and can guide data requesters' acceptance checks and third-party security assessments; it also sets assessment methods for each requirement, and its annexes give annotation examples and task types.

records.title: Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide — Guide to Security Emergency Response for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
records.original_title: 网络安全标准实践指南——生成式人工智能服务安全应急响应指南
records.short_title: TC260-PG-202515A (generative AI security emergency response)
records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: TC260 practice guide that implements the Interim Measures for generative AI services by giving providers a method to classify and grade generative AI service security incidents and an emergency response process. Incidents are information content, data security, cyberattack or other incidents, graded from level 1 (especially major) to level 4 (general). The process covers preparation (response team, plans, keyword and test-question banks, drills), monitoring (a refusal rate of at least 95% on the should-refuse test bank for hot events), handling, with service restriction or takedown and reporting of serious incidents to the competent department, and review.
records.notes: Version V1.0-202509, released with notice 网安秘字〔2025〕125号 dated 15 Sept 2025 and posted on 22 Sept 2025. A generative AI service security incident is defined as an event caused by human factors, malicious attacks or inherent model flaws that damages the service or its data and has negative effects on the state, society or economy. Classification and grading follow GB/T 20986-2023, and illegal and unhealthy information mainly means the 29 risks in Annex A (A.1 to A.4) of GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10). Self-assessed incidents of level 3 or higher with possible wide public impact are to be reported to the competent department immediately when they occur five times within 24 hours, affect more than 10,000 users and may cause adverse social impact; general incidents are handled internally and reported periodically. Annex A gives cases of a discrimination incident and a false-information incident.

records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: TC260 practice guide on the security of deploying and using agents: large-model-based AI agents for personal-assistant use that need high user permissions. For the assessment, preparation, deployment, use and decommissioning stages it advises against unmaintained projects and agents that open public interfaces automatically, and calls for installation materials from official channels, a separate device or isolated environment, large models that have completed generative AI service filing, no administrator rights, limited directories and network exposure, full logging, a high-risk operations list with second confirmation or blocking, and emergency stop.
records.notes: Version v1.0-202607, released with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕80号 of 1 July 2026. It can also guide the choice of commercial agent services. High-risk operations include stopping system services, formatting disks, bulk deletion, changing permissions, keys or firewall rules and accessing password managers, and may include transfers and payments. Annex A is a security checklist; Annex B gives organisations management guidance: an internal agent-use policy with prohibited behaviour and approval steps, an agent asset register, logging and risk analysis of agent activity, and discovery of unapproved agents on internal networks.

records.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
records.summary: TC260 practice guide on how individual users can use AI services over the internet securely. Users should recognise AI's limits such as errors and hallucinations, avoid over-reliance and replacing real social contact, and watch for misuse such as cloned voices of relatives or forged official notices. They should use services from regular channels and generative AI built on filed large models, check agreements and permissions, protect sensitive information, cross-check outputs, treat legal, medical or financial outputs as reference only, and not induce harmful outputs, impersonate others or remove AI content labels.

Guardians of minors and elderly users are asked to help them use AI services safely. records.original_title: AIインシデントレスポンス・アプローチブック
records.short_title: J-AISI AI Incident Response Approach Book (AI-IRS)
records.issuing_body: Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI)
records.summary: Framework of the Japan AI Safety Institute for responding to incidents caused by risks unique to AI systems, for executives such as Chief AI Officers and CISOs, security teams (CSIRTs, SOCs) and policymakers. Starting from the premise that AI incidents are inevitable, it stresses detective controls that minimise damage and presents the AI Incident Response System (AI-IRS), which adds observability (detection and analysis) and controllability (containment, eradication and recovery) to existing incident response. It analyses RAG systems and AI agents, links the approach to SBOM for AI and the NIST Cyber AI Profile, and calls for transparency and traceability across the AI supply chain.
records.notes: Published in Japanese and English, each with a summary edition. The book presents a conceptual framework that does not replace existing information security incident response frameworks such as NIST SP 800-61; implementation guides and procedures are to follow as related deliverables. It also discusses contractual 'action' by AI with reference to the UNCITRAL Model Law on Automated Contracting, sustained budgets for AI incident response, and gives a confirmation flow for the CAIO in an appendix.

records.title: Data Quality Management Guidebook: Maximizing the Value of Data and AI
records.short_title: J-AISI Data Quality Management Guidebook
records.issuing_body: Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI)
records.summary: Guidebook of the Japan AI Safety Institute on managing the quality of data used to build and operate AI systems, on the premise that poor data quality degrades AI performance and trust. It adds AI-specific points such as annotation quality, bias checks, drift management, synthetic data and monitoring.

The guidebook was produced by J-AISI's standards team with data experts of IPA's Digital Infrastructure Center and J-AISI's Data Quality Sub-Working Group, and is maintained as a living document.

records.title: Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety in the Healthcare Sector: Toward the Realization of Trustworthy AI
records.original_title: ヘルスケア領域におけるAIセーフティ評価観点ガイド
records.short_title: J-AISI Healthcare AI Safety Evaluation Guide
records.issuing_body: Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI), Healthcare Sub-Working Group of the Business Demonstration Working Group

records.summary: Guidelines of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications on technical measures that AI developers and AI providers can take to secure AI, mainly large language models and systems that contain them. records.summary: Government-wide rules, decided by the executive board of the Council for the Promotion of a Digital Society, for procuring and using generative AI in government information systems, to promote its use and manage its risks together. records.short_title: Slovak deceptive recordings bill (print 1266)
records.issuing_body: National Council of the Slovak Republic; private members' bill by MPs Andrej Danko, Karol Farkašovský, Dagmar Kramplová and Adam Lučanský
records.summary: Private members' bill on deceptive recordings, which its explanatory memorandum links to AI and digital tools that can create or alter images, sound and video so that they appear authentic. It would extend the Civil Code's consent-based protection of a person's likeness and personal expressions to recordings created or substantially altered by a technical process; make it a misdemeanour to make or share such a recording of another without consent where it can harm their honour, dignity or privacy; add such recordings that seriously threaten a person's standing or rights to the crime of dangerous electronic harassment; and extend criminal liability of legal persons to that crime.
records.notes: Received by the National Council on 27 March 2026 from MPs Andrej Danko, Karol Farkašovský, Dagmar Kramplová and Adam Lučanský. The Speaker proposed the Constitutional Law Committee as lead committee (decision no. 1336). By resolution no. 1497 of 5 May 2026 the National Council decided at first reading to consider the bill in second reading and assigned it to the Constitutional Law Committee as lead committee; the resolution sets the committee's deadline as the start of the plenary debate on the bill, while the print page gives 25 May 2026. By letter of 7 September 2026 the sponsors asked for the bill to be included in the session of the National Council beginning on 17 November 2026. The amendments: a new § 12(4) of the Civil Code; a new misdemeanour in § 49(1)(h) of the Misdemeanours Act, with the sanctions of § 49(2); a new § 360b(1)(c) of the Criminal Code (dangerous electronic harassment); and § 3 of the Act on criminal liability of legal persons. The bill would take effect on 1 January 2027.
records.scope_note: A private members' bill that amends the Civil Code, the Misdemeanours Act, the Criminal Code and the Act on criminal liability of legal persons rather than creating an AI-specific act; included because it is the operative instrument proposed against deceptive recordings made or altered with AI and other technical means (deepfakes).

records.issuing_body: National Council of the Slovak Republic; private members' bill by MPs František Mikloško and Igor Janckulík
records.summary: Private members' bill against misuse of AI-generated synthetic content (deepfakes). It would give everyone a Civil Code right to protect their 'digital identity' (likeness, voice and other identifiable traits) from unauthorised use in synthetic content, lasting 50 years after death; make creating or spreading another's deepfake without consent a misdemeanour (fine up to EUR 250) and, if seriously harmful, a crime with up to two years' prison, more for sexual content, election interference or depictions of children; oblige hosting providers to take notices and remove manifestly illegal synthetic content within 24 hours (fines up to EUR 500,000); and add fast court interim measures.
records.notes: Received by the National Council on 25 September 2025 from MPs František Mikloško and Igor Janckulík; the Speaker proposed the Constitutional Law Committee (lead) and the Committee for Human Rights and National Minorities. The bill would have added § 11a to the Civil Code, § 49(1)(h) to the Misdemeanours Act, § 6 to the Electronic Commerce Act, § 374a to the Criminal Code (one to five years' imprisonment for substantial damage, a sexual motive or pornographic form, or intent to influence elections, a referendum or the integrity of public debate; three to eight years for synthetic content depicting a child or a person appearing to be a child), § 325a to the Civil Contentious Procedure Code and § 118a to the Copyright Act, under which realistic digitally generated imitations of a performance or of any person's appearance or voice could not be made public without consent, except clearly and permanently labelled fiction used for parody, satire, art or science. records.title: Resolution No. 12.677 approving the Operational Policy establishing guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence systems in the Judiciary (Version 1)
records.original_title: Política Operacional que establece directrices para el uso de sistemas de inteligencia artificial en el Poder Judicial
records.short_title: Paraguay judiciary AI use policy (CSJ Resolution 12.677)
records.issuing_body: Supreme Court of Justice of Paraguay (Corte Suprema de Justicia)
records.summary: Policy of Paraguay's Supreme Court of Justice guiding magistrates and judicial staff on the ethical, responsible and transparent use of AI systems, covering existing and future systems developed in-house, acquired or licensed. Under a principle of human oversight it lists permitted supporting uses and forbids delegating decisions to AI, fully automating processes that affect fundamental rights, and using AI to determine guilt or set penalties. Parties must be told when AI is used, generative-AI text must be disclosed and prompts documented, and opaque systems are banned. Further rules cover non-discrimination, personal data protection and security, and AI literacy training.
records.notes: Approved by Resolution No. 12.677 of 4 March 2026 after review of the policy recorded in Minute No. 11 of 20 November 2025 of the technical team of the Internal Control Committee, under Strategic Objective 3 of the Judiciary's Institutional Strategic Plan 2026-2030 and the MECIP:2015 internal-control standard. The resolution authorises the policy's application and sets no separate commencement date.
